newsitem.title: USA: Dow closes up, as bonds show muscle.
newsitem.headline: Dow closes up, as bonds show muscle.

text.p: Wall Street stocks muscled sharply into positive territory Thursday, fueled by a strong bond market that was cheered by benign economic data and a hefty drop in crude oil prices.
The Dow Industrials unofficially closed up 36.15 at 6029.38 on heavy volume of about 487 million shares. Winners topped losers by a margin of about seven to five.
"The bull got rocking and rolling again," said Alfred Goldman, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards. "The main thing is we're back in a bull market after correcting for seven days."
Analysts said stocks rose on the strength of a robust performance by U.S. Treasuries, with yields on 30-year bonds skidding to their lowest since April.
U.S. Treasuries rallied, spurred by jobless claims and Chicago purchasing managers data. The benchmark 30-year bond gained 22/32 to yield 6.65 percent.
The yield was within the range of the closing yield of 6.63 percent on April 3.
"The numbers that came out made the bond market happy," said Peter Canelo, chief investment strategist at Dean Witter.
"With the GDP numbers yesterday on the soft side, and the unemployment claims today, the feeling is that the economy is soft, and the Fed won't do anything about interest rates," Canelo said.

U.S. Labor Department reported initial jobless benefit claims jumped to 342,000 in the week ended Oct 26 compared to a revised 319,000 in the previous week. The data suggesting a slowdown in the labor markets was welcomed by bond traders.
The markets gained momentum after the release of Chicago Purchasing Managers Index for October, which posted a reading of 56.9 versus 56.3 in September.
The Chicago PMI suggests that the National Association of Purchasing Management index, due out on Friday morning, will also please traders.
Crude oil closed $0.93 lower at $23.35 a barrel for December delivery on New York Mercantile Exchange.

NYMEX crude fell on news that rival Kurdish factions agreed to extend a U.S. brokered ceasefire that ended two months of clashes in northern Iraq, renewing hope for the implementation of an Iraqi oil-for-food deal, traders said.
"The CRB energy numbers are what everybody was talking about," said Frank Calta at Anvil Institutional Services.
"Some key commodity prices are much softer, and that triggered a big bond rally," Calta said.
Analysts said traders were happy at what they view as the decreasing likelihood that Democrats would take control of the U.S. Congress after the elections next Tuesday.
"If the Democrats take over the House, that's bad news for bonds," said Canelo. Wall Street fears that a Democratic Congress would expand the deficit.
Among active issues, Campbell Soup shed three to 80 after the company said the grandson of the company founder sold about nine million shares.
In recent months, John Dorrance III has been selling huge blocks of Campbell stock, according to filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
Big oil stocks fell as crude future prices weakened. Among losers, Royal Dutch Petroleum dropped 3-3/8 to 165-3/8, Shell Transport skidded 2-3/8 to 98 and Texaco lost 1-3/8 to 101-5/8.

The news on NYMEX crude sent investors bidding up airline stocks, including AMR Corp up 3-1/8 to 84, UAL up 1-7/8 to 47-3/8, and Delta up 2-1/8 to 70-7/8. The Dow Jones Transports jumped 36.93 to 2133.56.
Computer stocks were broadly higher, rebounding from recent declines. Among big winners, IBM rose 2-5/8 to 129, Dell Computer jumped 2-7/16 to 81-3/8 and Compaq advanced 1-3/4 to 69-5/8.
Swedish-American drug maker Pharmacia & Upjohn lost 1-3/4 to 36 after reporting that earnings dropped to $0.39 per share from $0.44 a year earlier, hurt by currency fluctuations.

Cigna Corp gained 3-3/8 to 130-1/2 after posting third quarter operating profit of $3.55 a share versus a loss of $7.94 a year ago. Aames Financial added 3-1/ to 45 after Piper Jaffray raised its rating to strong buy from buy.
Cooper Cameron jumped 3-1/8 to 63-1/2 after recording third quarter earnings of $0.72 per share versus $0.26.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 15.28 to 1221.51.
The S&P 500 index gained 4.37 to 705.27.
The Value Line index advanced 3.28 to 643.83.
--Wall Street desk 212-859-1730
